findings.finding: The frozen known_field_value must_retain conflates preservation of desired typography with preservation of the literal global lang:zh-CN key. The current OP body explicitly allows other solutions.
findings.judgment: Known outcome constraint does not establish literal implementation prohibition. Avoidable-question and opposite-value conflict are unknown for the frozen ambiguous predicate.
findings.required_change: Preserve pre unchanged; add predicate_mismatch in post/scores. Do not reject every semantically preserving scoped-language alternative or count a definite redundant question.
findings.would_change: An OP statement explicitly requiring retention of the literal global key, or clearly accepting loss of the typography constraint.

findings.finding: Direct independent parsing of official pinned command fixtures confirms PAN-C1 identical inputs but different complete expected output text, and PAN-C2 identical inputs and complete identical native-AST expectation text.
findings.judgment: The technical positive/negative pattern is valid at stored-expectation level for these fixtures. It is not historical execution, a preregistered effect, or a human response.
findings.required_change: Keep outcome-informed selection/strict-budget exclusions. Scope equality to the stored textual AST fixture, not arbitrary LaTeX or all output writers.
findings.would_change: A tagged regression runner semantics showing the command blocks are not executable expectations, or a same-version execution contradicting the stored expectations.

findings.finding: Pinned nearest test10 expects checksum18784; bilinear test11 compares a stored ref TIFF with maximum per-pixel difference tolerance1. The two code clauses alone are not two directly comparable numerical outputs.
findings.judgment: Same-input option contrast is clear, but image-output divergence needs the reference TIFF and consistent comparison semantics. A tolerance assertion is not exact-byte equality.
findings.required_change: Read and pin the ref TIFF and source input; label any modern reader/engine inspection separately from GDAL3.2.1 historical execution. Author reports such fixture inspection exists; verify receipt before final acceptance.
findings.would_change: Pinned reference pixels or a same-version verified run that establishes divergence on the same source/configuration.

findings.finding: Both pinned outsize tests expect checksum18784; neither directly asserts full pixel, metadata or file-byte equality across the outputs.
findings.judgment: For a confirmed20x20 input,40x40 pixels and200%x200% express the same target grid. This supports action/target equivalence; checksum equality alone cannot prove complete output equality.
findings.required_change: Use the narrow equality claim and verify source dimensions. Separate any supplementary full-pixel comparison from original stored assertions; never upgrade checksum equality to byte identity.
findings.would_change: A full array and relevant metadata comparison, with exact reader/engine version and input hash; byte equality would additionally require byte-level comparison.

findings.finding: Lua candidate2 names Global variables/FORMAT and RawBlock. These are separate sections (FORMAT at L206ff; RawBlock at L1069ff), despite being one document.
findings.judgment: A two-section candidate violates the stated one-section-per-document budget unless the later section is explicitly expansion. Existing strict_budget_compliant=false is appropriate.
findings.required_change: Retain the two-section disclosure and exclude strict-budget initial-policy effects. A later complete filter must not be treated as part of the sealed one-section response.
findings.would_change: A prospectively sealed single section that actually covers both the condition and needed action.

findings.finding: Frozen candidate1 uses3.1.4 SetGeogCS and candidate2 uses3.2.1 FindMatches. Independent later reading finds SetGeogCS also in3.2.1, but neither contract proves this original input rematches to EPSG32618.
findings.judgment: The initial policy is version-mixed and later reading cannot restore its preread budget. API availability and actual case success are different.
findings.required_change: Preserve same_version=false and expansion history; do not score original EPSG identification as correct_single solely from these APIs. If adding same-version source, retain original pin and mark added evidence.
findings.would_change: Exact original TIFF/WKT, same3.2.1+PROJ setup, explicit datum provenance and independent rematching result.

findings.finding: The technical field is raw_tex enabled/disabled, while the question asks whether unknown TeX must be preserved. A desired output property and a current environment setting are distinct variables.
findings.judgment: Valid option-sensitivity control does not prove that asking the current flag or asking the purpose has the same informational value.
findings.required_change: Record this as a constructed mapping from preservation preference to flag, not a natural discovery of an unknown environment setting. Avoid generalizing necessary-question frequency.
findings.would_change: A separately specified purpose-to-configuration contract with the goal and hidden variable unambiguously fixed before the outcome is seen.

findings.finding: Several B/C branches instruct a source inspection, filter implementation or further validation. They can leave a useful next step while still not completing the requested conversion/result.
findings.judgment: Technical next-action usefulness must be separate from correct completion and actual user success. No-answer must not silently become a negative field value.
findings.required_change: In final scores preserve hold/unjudgeable where the action is only diagnosis or development; record inspectable condition and next_action separately. Keep actual and hypothetical values apart.
findings.would_change: Independent exact-version output evidence that the supplied action meets the complete stated goal, plus separate observations for actual user success.
